solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Hot stew from Pret is trendy

parts.note: H is the standard abbreviation for hot, as on a tap

indicators.note: a stew is a jumble cooked together, so the letters of the following words are mixed up

explanation.surface: A café's hot stew is declared fashionable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stew' looks like a dish from the Pret sandwich chain, but with 'from' it signals the shuffle.
explanation.definitionFit: A hipster is a person who follows the latest fashions, hence a trendy one; the word works as an adjective too.

clue.text: Excitement mounted in Sleepy Hollow

indicators.note: mounted says the hidden letters are read backwards
the clue word that says the letters sit inside the next words

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A thrill climbs inside the spooky village of Sleepy Hollow.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'mounted' means read upwards: EPYH, inside 'Sleepy Hollow', turned round.
explanation.definitionFit: Hype is overblown publicity or the excitement whipped up by it.

clue.text: Oscar speech curtailed after big player turned critical

indicators.note: after puts the speech pieces behind the turned big player
turned tells us to write the important person's letters backwards

parts.note: a VIP is a very important person, a big player
Oscar is O in the NATO phonetic alphabet

indicators.note: curtailed means cut off at the tail, so the last letter goes

parts.note: a talk is a speech

explanation.surface: An Oscar acceptance speech cut short after a star turned out decisive.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turned' makes PIV from VIP; 'curtailed' cuts TALK to TAL.
explanation.definitionFit: Pivotal and critical are synonyms: both describe something on which everything else turns.

clue.text: Go to bed with doctor to nurse you now at the door

parts.note: to turn in is to go to bed

indicators.note: to nurse is to hold close, so the doctor's letters enclose the next piece

parts.note: a GP is a general practitioner, a family doctor
U is text-speak for you

explanation.surface: A suggestive invitation to bed with a doctor, interrupted by someone at the door.
explanation.walkthrough: The racy surface hides a plain charade; 'to nurse' signals one piece holding another, and the definition describes someone arriving.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone turning up is arriving, so is just now at the door.

clue.text: Unnerve farm animals using cleaver's other end

indicators.note: using signals that one letter is swapped in to replace another

parts.note: cattle are farm animals

indicators.note: cleaver begins with the letter the farm animals also begin with, and its other end supplies the replacement

explanation.surface: A butcher frightens livestock by wielding the wrong end of a cleaver.
explanation.walkthrough: CATTLE starts with C, as 'cleaver' does; swap in cleaver's 'other end', R.
explanation.definitionFit: To rattle someone is to fluster or disconcert them, synonymous with unnerve.

clue.text: Subcontract beginning in March to drill well offshore?

indicators.note: to drill is to bore into, so the March letter is put into the other piece

parts.note: far out is well out to sea, with the question mark admitting a playful reading

indicators.note: beginning in picks out the first letter of March

explanation.surface: An oil firm contracts out the drilling of an offshore well starting in March.
explanation.walkthrough: The oil-rig picture hides that 'well' is an adverb here, part of a phrase meaning a long way out to sea.
explanation.definitionFit: To farm out work is to hand it to others to do, which is what subcontracting means.

clue.text: Properly selected victims show willing

parts.note: a show, such as an agricultural show, is a fair
game means willing, as in 'game for anything'

explanation.surface: Victims are chosen properly and put on a willing show.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Properly' looks like the source of FAIR, but it belongs to the definition; FAIR comes from 'show'.
explanation.definitionFit: Fair game means a legitimate target for attack or ridicule, people it is proper to pick on.

clue.text: Unusual club banning tango steps from Cuba

parts.note: rum means odd or unusual

indicators.note: banning means the tango letter is kept out of the club's letters

parts.note: a bat is a club, as in cricket or baseball
Tango is T in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A strange nightclub forbids the tango but allows Cuban dance steps.
explanation.walkthrough: 'banning' takes T from BAT to leave BA.
explanation.definitionFit: The rumba is a dance of Cuban origin, so its moves are steps from Cuba.

clue.text: Half of pitch not in use someone correcting flaws is rolling

parts.note: a machine switched off is not in use

indicators.note: rolling turns over, so the following letters are written backwards

parts.note: ED is short for editor, the person correcting errors in copy

explanation.surface: Part of a sports field is unused while a groundsman fixing bumps rolls it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rolling' turns ED IS into SIDE. The off side is the half of a cricket field facing the batter's bat.
explanation.definitionFit: In cricket the field is split into the off side and the leg side, so this is one half of the pitch area.

clue.text: Weak point limiting soldier's real quality

indicators.note: limiting means enclosing, so the soldier's letters are put inside

parts.note: thin means weak, as in a thin excuse
a ness is a headland or point of land
GI is an American soldier

explanation.surface: A frail spot holds a soldier's genuine character.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Weak point' reads as one idea, a flaw, but splits into two words; 'limiting' then has them enclose the soldier.
explanation.definitionFit: Thinginess is the quality of being a real, physical thing, its concrete actuality.

clue.text: Errors repeatedly uncovered in yearly tax return of Italian singer

parts.note: PA is per annum, Latin for yearly

indicators.note: in places the stripped errors inside the tax

parts.note: VAT is value added tax

indicators.note: uncovered strips the outer letters, and repeatedly does it twice to the word errors
return of means the vermouth letters are read backwards

parts.note: It is short for Italian vermouth, as in gin and It

explanation.surface: Repeated mistakes surface in an Italian tenor's annual tax return.
explanation.walkthrough: 'repeatedly uncovered' strips ERRORS twice to RO, which goes 'in' VAT; 'return of' turns IT to TI.
explanation.definitionFit: Luciano Pavarotti was the celebrated operatic tenor, one of the most famous vocalists of his era.

clue.text: Nearly all smoke after sex, reflecting informal habit

indicators.note: reflecting gives a mirror image, so the combined letters run backwards
after puts the smoke after the sex piece

parts.note: it is a coy word for sex appeal or sex

indicators.note: nearly all drops the final letter

parts.note: fume is smoke or vapour

explanation.surface: Someone muses over a post-coital cigarette and their casual clothing.
explanation.walkthrough: The habit is clothing, not smoking; 'reflecting' turns the whole run of letters round, giving the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Mufti is plain civilian dress worn by someone usually in uniform, so informal clothing; habit means dress.

clue.text: Member relaxing on journey three sheets to the wind?

indicators.note: on means placed after, so the member and relaxing follow the journey

parts.note: a trip is a journey
a leg is a limb or member
lazing means relaxing idly

explanation.surface: A drunk lounges about on a trip, three sheets to the wind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Three sheets to the wind' means drunk, but read literally it is three panes of glass set against the weather.
explanation.definitionFit: Triple glazing uses three panes of glass, sheets that face the wind outside, so the question mark flags a literal reading.

clue.text: Impressive class doing no work bags top grades

parts.note: a form is a school class

indicators.note: bags means holds inside, so the grades go into the idle piece

parts.note: idle means doing no work
A and B are the top exam grades

explanation.surface: A lazy class still somehow gets top grades, which is impressive.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bags' is a verb meaning grabs or holds, not a noun about luggage.
explanation.definitionFit: Formidable means inspiring awe or respect through size or power, much as impressive does.

clue.text: Do favours for old balding men every so often

indicators.note: every so often takes alternate letters of the words balding men, starting with the first

explanation.surface: Doing favours for elderly men going bald now and then.
explanation.walkthrough: 'every so often' picks B, L, I, G, E from 'balding men'.
explanation.definitionFit: To oblige someone is to do them a favour or service, the same as doing favours for them.

clue.text: Small fly continually bit

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for small, as on clothing labels
a midge is a small fly
on means continually, as in 'went on and on'

explanation.surface: A small fly kept biting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bit' looks like a verb about the fly but is the noun definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A smidgeon is a tiny amount, a little bit of something.

clue.text: Fellow collects carpet rod for major junk dealer

indicators.note: collects means gathers in, so the fellow's letters surround the others

parts.note: a don is a fellow of a university college
a rug is a small carpet
a bar is a rod

explanation.surface: A college fellow gathers a carpet and curtain rod for a big rubbish dealer.
explanation.walkthrough: Junk is slang for hard drugs such as heroin, not rubbish; 'collects' has the fellow enclose both items.
explanation.definitionFit: A drug baron is a major trafficker, and junk is slang for heroin, so he deals junk on a large scale.

clue.text: Dreadful people parking on playing field

parts.note: P is the symbol for parking

indicators.note: playing means the letters of field are moved about

explanation.surface: Awful people are parking on the playing field.
explanation.walkthrough: 'playing' rearranges FIELD into DLIFE.
explanation.definitionFit: Pond life is an insulting term for people regarded as the lowest of the low, contemptible people.

clue.text: Own goal perhaps upset team pro, you hear

indicators.note: upset means knocked over and disordered, so the letters of team are rearranged
you hear signals that a word is spoken rather than spelt

parts.note: pro means for, in favour of

explanation.surface: A team professional upset at an own goal, as you hear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' turns TEAM into META; 'you hear' gives PHOR, sounding like FOR. 'perhaps' marks own goal as one example.
explanation.definitionFit: Calling a self-inflicted setback an own goal is a figure of speech, an example of a metaphor.

clue.text: Male pet snake fed locusts, primarily — 5 down?

parts.note: a tom is a male cat, a common pet

indicators.note: fed means given something to swallow, so the locusts letter goes inside the snake

parts.note: a boa is a constricting snake

indicators.note: primarily picks the first letter of locusts

explanation.surface: A tomcat and a pet snake are given locusts to eat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fed' puts L inside BOA. 5 down is FAIR GAME, read here as a game at a fair.
explanation.definitionFit: A tombola is a lottery-style raffle game commonly run at fairs and fetes, so a fair game.

clue.text: Unsettled US job market's facing high fliers going abroad

indicators.note: unsettled means disturbed, so the following letters are rearranged
the facing of the market is its front, so take its first letter

explanation.surface: An unsettled American jobs market sends high-flying executives abroad.
explanation.walkthrough: The M (front of 'market's') joins US JOB in the mix. 'High fliers' suggests successful people but means aircraft.
explanation.definitionFit: Jumbos are jumbo jets, large airliners that fly high on long-haul routes abroad.

clue.text: Wrap it in gold and buff up

indicators.note: in places the it letters inside the reversed pair
up in a down clue means the letters are written from bottom to top

parts.note: or is gold in heraldry
to rub is to buff or polish

explanation.surface: An instruction to wrap something in gold leaf and polish it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' reverses ORRUB to BURRO, and 'in' places IT inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A burrito is a Mexican tortilla wrapped round a filling, a type of wrap.

clue.text: Shake case that might contain bolts

definitions.meaning: a case for crossbow bolts or arrows carried by an archer

explanation.surface: Trembling over a box of loose bolts.
explanation.definitionFit: To quiver is to tremble; a quiver is also an archer's case holding arrows or crossbow bolts.

clue.text: Film of dirt turned diamonds on ring brown

indicators.note: on means placed after in an across clue
turned means the dirt word is reversed

parts.note: mud is dirt
a band is a ring
D is the abbreviation for diamonds in card games
umber is an earthy brown pigment

explanation.surface: A film of dirt and a brown ring left on diamonds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turned' makes DUM from MUD. Dumb and Dumber is a 1994 Jim Carrey comedy film.
explanation.definitionFit: Dumb and Dumber is a 1994 Hollywood comedy movie, an example of a film.

clue.text: Have gremlins sheared each sheep?

indicators.note: sheared means clipped at both ends, leaving the middle letters

parts.note: a tup is a ram, a male sheep

explanation.surface: A farmer wonders whether every sheep has been shorn.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sheared' trims EACH to AC.
explanation.definitionFit: A machine that acts up malfunctions, as if gremlins were at work in it.

clue.text: Marzipan one includes in short order

indicators.note: includes says the answer is contained within the words marzipan one

explanation.surface: One marzipan treat contains something, very soon.
explanation.walkthrough: 'includes' points to the letters across the join of 'marzipAN ONe'.
explanation.definitionFit: Anon is an old word for soon or shortly, so in short order.

clue.text: Improve footwear with twisted heel

indicators.note: twisted heel turns round the last two letters, the heel of the word

parts.note: boots are footwear

explanation.surface: Upgrading shoes by fitting a twisted heel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'twisted heel' swaps the final TS of BOOTS to ST.
explanation.definitionFit: To boost something is to raise or improve it.

clue.text: Flipping S over N in one?

definitions.text: Flipping S over N in one?

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one

indicators.note: flipping means turning over, so the letters that follow are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: Turning a compass so south sits above north.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flipping' scrambles S, OVER, N, IN and I together. Putting south above north is turning the map upside down.
explanation.definitionFit: An inversion is a turning upside down, exactly what putting south over north does.

clue.text: Test nuclear reactor ignoring current model

parts.note: an exam is a test

indicators.note: ignoring means the current letter is left out

parts.note: a pile is an early name for a nuclear reactor
I is the symbol for electric current

explanation.surface: Testing a nuclear reactor while disregarding the current model.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ignoring' removes I from PILE to leave PLE.
explanation.definitionFit: An example is a model or pattern to follow.

clue.text: Brief race to the bottom

parts.note: to run is to race
down means to the bottom

explanation.surface: The economy's race to the bottom.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Brief' is a noun: a quick summary, the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A rundown is a brief summary or report of the main points.
